card.band: 8h. Bitstream-exact Edgebreaker with valence contexts and the prediction schemes is a deep dependency chain; frontier agents get decode right in some trials but miss encoder-side bit-exactness and the normal/texcoord schemes. Buckets: connectivity decode, connectivity encode, each prediction scheme, point-cloud paths. A weaker model stops at decode of simple meshes.
card.cheat: Calling a system libdraco or copying prebuilt .drc: no libdraco in the image, only the stripped source; hidden meshes are unseen and the graded encoder output is checked by the sealed decoder.
card.grading: Hidden gtest-style cases and generated OBJ/PLY meshes: decode of reference .drc files must match exact vertex/face/attribute values, and re-encoded output must round-trip through a sealed reference decoder. Credit is the fraction of cases passed over what the reference passes. Existing in-tree tests are the visible sample.
card.reference: The upstream implementation at the pinned release, with the removed files as the reference diff (expected well over 1500 lines).
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot of Draco with the Edgebreaker connectivity encoder/decoder and the mesh prediction schemes (parallelogram, constrained multi-parallelogram, texcoord portable, geometric normal) removed behind their existing interfaces. The agent rebuilds them so the library builds and the draco_encoder/draco_decoder CLIs work.

full_card.band: 8h tier as seeded looks too short for the full scope. Estimated frontier effort about 14h for the whole scope. Prefer tier 20h, or narrow to connectivity decode and encode with parallelogram and tex-portable to fit 8h. Partial buckets: connectivity decode (standard), connectivity decode (valence), encode, each prediction scheme, point-cloud path. Weaker model likely stops at simple-mesh decode.
full_card.build_cost: Reference is the public upstream code, so writing it is cheap; cost is the sealed harness, mesh generator, reference decoder, and checking the snapshot builds offline. About 3-4 days.
full_card.deliverable: Library that builds offline plus draco_encoder and draco_decoder CLIs; Edgebreaker standard and valence connectivity, prediction schemes (parallelogram, constrained multi-parallelogram, tex-coords portable, geometric normal), and point-cloud paths.
full_card.gates_anticheat: No system libdraco or DracoPy wheel in the image (purge Debian libdraco and pip DracoPy, check find_package paths); sealed decoder and hidden meshes outside image; no copying prebuilt .drc; build config and tests are read-only for grading; history removed.

Size not yet measured; plausibly tens to low hundreds of cases unless the generator is scaled up.

spike_plan.kill_if: Submodules missing or build red offline, the suite is flaky across runs, or the removed set is under about 500 lines (then re-scope or kill K3).
spike_plan.pass_if: Upstream builds offline in under about 30 min with submodules, the suite is deterministic over three runs, removed set is at least 1500 non-blank lines, and the stripped tree breaks the build or fails tests.
steps: In a throwaway container with network, clone google/draco at tag 1.5.9 with --recurse-submodules and check the four submodules are populated.
Build the unmodified tree with CMake and C++17, time it, and run ./build/draco_tests --gtest_color=no three times; record pass count and any flaky tests.
Use the built draco_encoder on 3-5 OBJ/PLY meshes (plain, with normals, with texcoords) and draco_decoder to round-trip; save the .drc outputs as sample hidden-style cases.
In a copy, delete mesh_edgebreaker_*.{h,cc} and the four prediction scheme sources and count the removed non-blank lines; confirm the removed set is at least 1500 lines.
Check the stripped copy fails to link or build, so the grading surface depends on the removed code.
Confirm no libdraco is resolved from system paths in the stripped build (ldd and find_package output), and check Debian libdraco-dev is absent from the target image.

v1.summary: Draco 1.5.9 is a real, Apache-2.0 upstream release, and its Edgebreaker and prediction-scheme sources exist at the pinned tag, so the seed passes the paper-trail gate. The main risks are that a frontier model may recall the public C++ (and a Rust partial port exists), that an 8h tier is short for roughly 14h of full scope, and that the smoke build has not run, so the spike must confirm the offline build and the 1500-line removal before any cost is committed.

v2.note: Strongest card in the batch. The release, licence and every target source file are confirmed at 1.5.9. Use the 20h tier: 14 frontier hours does not fit 8h. Grading accepts any valid implementation: decode is checked for exact values on reference .drc files, and encoder output only has to round-trip through the sealed decoder. Open risks: the removed-line count is unmeasured, the offline build with submodules is unverified (smoke_build is empty), and Debian libdraco-dev and DracoPy wheels must be kept out of the image. Band is capped at 3 because there is no dated evidence. The draco-oxide link is dead. The draco-core Rust port is public, but no run-time path exists if crates are not vendored.
